prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 218px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 147px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 1235px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 62px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 599px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 598px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 599px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A catalogue of accredited training courses: readers browse course names, compare duration and fee, and use the description for detail before choosing.","reading":"Right-to-left and row-first: the rightmost course name is the entry point, then duration and trainer, then the long description, with the fee at the far left as a quick check. Comparison is mainly identity plus duration/fee; description is read only after a row interests the reader.","groups":["cols 1 and 5: identity and price are the primary decision anchors and benefit from staying intact","cols 2 and 3: short logistics metadata that play the same compact supporting role","col 4: long prose description, functionally separate from the scannable metadata"],"keep_intact":["col 1 course names: no mid-word breaks; longest unbreakable word is 58px","col 5 fee values: keep as one line/one token; 62px content width","col 2 numerals and units: keep numbers with their units where possible","col 3 trainer names: keep honorific/title with the name where possible"],"may_wrap":["col 4 description: prose, expected to wrap over many lines","col 1 long course names: wrap at spaces between words","col 2 duration phrases: wrap between number and unit or before parenthetical hours","col 3 trainer names: wrap between title and name parts"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[130,80,75,230,83],"idea":"Description-led: give the only long prose field most of the width so row height stays controlled, while compact metadata wraps within that same height."},{"name":"B","widths":[239,75,70,131,83],"idea":"Identity-and-fee anchored: keep course names and fees fully intact for fast recognition and price comparison, letting duration, trainer and description absorb the squeeze."},{"name":"C","widths":[150,115,100,150,83],"idea":"Logistics-led: widen duration and trainer so the operational metadata scans almost as whole labels, accepting heavier wrapping in course names and descriptions."}]}
